actor.name: Viv Ansanm (Haitian gang coalition)
actor.seat: Port-au-Prince (territorial stronghold in the metropolitan area; no single capital)

stances.note: Viv Ansanm (Haitian gang coalition) has not written its reading of Haiti; the atlas mirrors Haiti's 'adversary' reading as 'adversary' at low confidence, on the same evidence. Bond and trend are not assessed from this side.

sources.title: UN renews Haiti force mandate for six months after fresh gang killings

stances_toward.note: Viv Ansanm, formed in September 2023 by G9 and G-Pèp, was created to attack the Haitian government (police stations, government buildings, infrastructure) and to fight the international force (Wikipedia, tier 4). Adversary is our reading, not a source's word, and it is the rare grade by design: the sources show hostile attacks on the state, not a stated aim of replacing it, so if a stricter reading is taken this becomes rival. Bond none: no kinship or affinity is named. Trend stable: the 2026 coverage shows continued killings, with no sign of a turn.

relations_from.summary: Armed gang members ambushed Salvadoran Air Force personnel serving with the Gang Suppression Force in Port-au-Prince with gunfire and explosives; four Salvadoran service members were missing after escaping their burning armoured vehicle.

sources.title: Four Salvadoran air force members missing after gang ambush in Haiti

relations_from.summary: Gangs ambushed a Salvadoran Air Force armoured vehicle on 18 Oct and took four Salvadoran technicians, attached to the international Gang Suppression Force, hostage. The portal reports it on 21 Oct.

relations_to.summary: Retake Port-au-Prince from Viv Ansanm, the gang alliance formed in September 2023 by G9 and G-Pèp, with the Gang Suppression Force; read as the aim of the transition government (C). The force's strength and the gangs' reach are in the rows of the GSF and the Kenyan contingent.
